Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  November 6, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on November 6, 2025. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Cynthia
  McLemore - District 3, Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4,
  Absent:  Commissioner Octavio Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Kaderick Burns  Recreation Supervisor
  Marisela Mansour  Human Services Program Manager of Operations
  Brian McClure  Parks Administration Superintendent
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and second by Commissioner Beck
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on October 7,
2025, be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, McLemore, and Beck
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Parks Administration Superintendent Brian McClure
reported the following: Parks Division - Park staff have installed new windscreens,
benches, and shade canopies at the pickleball courts in Darby Park. The small baseball field
at Rogers Park has been over seeded in preparation for the winter baseball season. New
park rules signs will soon be installed at the entrances of each park. Graffiti Division - In
August, staff experienced heavy activity in the following areas: Vincent Park, West
Boulevard from Hyde Park to Florence Avenue and District 3: on Arbor Vitae to the La
Cienega corridor. Tree Division - WCA wrapping up annual contract and working on
projects at the Water treatment plant, Vincent Park, and Hillcrest Boulevard. Centinela

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Adobe Museum, and Siminski Park. City crews are doing service requests along with
additional trimming projects on Manchester (palms), La Brea (Ficus) and Centinela Adobe
Museum. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Kaderick Burns reported the following:
Youth Sports - The start of fall represents the beginning of a new year in Inglewood Youth
Sports. The Inglewood Rams flag football season always gets the league moving with a
bang offering 4 age divisions, 22 teams, 285 participants, and 25 coaches. In addition, the
league has 34 girls participating which is the highest number of female players in the last
5 years. The oldest age group (Prep Division 11-12) play Thursday Nights at 5:45 pm and
6:45 pm. The remaining divisions play on Saturday’s at the newly renovated Champions
Field from 9:00 am through 3:00 pm. The league focuses on learning the game,
fundamental development, and having fun in competition. The season runs through the
first weekend in December concluding with championship games, awards, and team
parties. This year, Inglewood will host the SCMAF tournament for the A Division (3 rd & 4th
graders) and D Division (7th & 8th graders) on December 13 and 14. Flag football teams
from Bakersfield to San Diego will travel to Inglewood and compete for the coveted
Southern California Municipal Athletic Federation championships. Come out and support
our Inglewood youth. You won’t be disappointed as the action is fast, fun, and
entertaining. Winter sports registration for soccer and basketball begin December first on
our youth sports website at cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com. Turkey Giveaway - City of
Inglewood’s Annual Turkey Giveaway will take place on Tuesday, November 25, 2025 from
9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at Hollywood Park. This is a drive-through event only, and pre-
registration is required, no walk-ups will be permitted. Individuals wishing to participate
may register by visiting tinyurl.com/INGTURKEY2025. The event flyer will be available on
the City’s website beginning Monday, November 10. Residents are encouraged to visit the
website, scan the QR code, or click the registration link to sign up. Christmas tree Lighting
- Join us for the City of Inglewood’s Annual Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony! [The
celebration will take place on Wednesday, December 3, 2025 from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m. at the
Kia Forum. The evening will begin with a holiday parade at 5:00 p.m., traveling along Prairie
Avenue from the Intuit Dome to the Kia Forum. Upon arrival at the Forum, guests will
enjoy live entertainment, a snow play area, arts and crafts, face painting, balloon artists,
game trucks, and much more! We invite the entire community to join us for this joyful,
family-friendly event as we kick off the holiday season in the City of Inglewood! For more
information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website at:
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Operations Manager Marisela Mansour
reported on the following: Senior Center Trips and Activities - Our Senior Center continues
to grow, with a diverse range of exciting presentations and activities planned for this
month.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

    On November 4, we will be taking seniors to the Culver City Farmer’s Market from
  2:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.
    On November 5, the Inglewood Inspirational Choir is having a special anniversary
  performance for our seniors 10:00 a.m. to 10:30 a.m.
    Alzheimer’s Los Angeles will be conducting a presentation on “Healthy Heart and
  Brain” On November 14.
    The Center for Health Care Rights will be conducting a presentation on “Navigating
  Medicare Together: A, B, C’s and D’s of Medicare” on November 12.
    On November 12, we will be taking seniors to El Camino College for a special “Spa
  Day” which includes hair, nails, and facials.
    LA County Department of Mental Health will be conducting a presentation on “Grief
  and Loss” on November 17.
    On November 20, we will be celebrating birthday’s for the months of August,
  September, October, November, and December) from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. on
  October 31.
Elderly Nutrition Program - The Senior Center serves approximately 460 seniors per week
through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals. We
continue to offer fresh produce on a weekly basis in partnership with the Social Justice
Learning Institute, as well as monthly shelf-stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los
Angeles Food Bank. Farmers' Market cards have been distributed, and seniors have been
able to take several trips to the market from the center through our transportation
services. We also work in partnership with Los Angeles County to refer seniors to our
center to receive Home Delivered Meals and workshops focused on healthy eating habits.
Through this same meal program, we provide our seniors with nourishing meals while they
are on field trips organized by the senior center, thanks to the support of our
transportation and operations managers. As our numbers continue to climb weekly in
program participation, we look forward to serving all of our seniors. Senior Transportation
Program - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to provide trips to
seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. We recently hired a full
time bus operator who is acclimating well. We are also in the process of hiring on a part
time bus operator so that we continue providing outstanding paratransit service to our
seniors and our disabled community. Our services will be closed for the city’s holiday
observance of Veteran’s Day, which is Tuesday, November 11 as well as the Thanksgiving
Holiday on, Thursday, November 27 and Friday, November 28. Those that are interested
in booking trips after the holidays should book their trips before the mentioned days to
ensure their trips are reserved.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director
Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Annual Thanksgiving Luncheon for seniors at

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

Intuit Dome - The Community Services Division will be taking Inglewood seniors to the
annual Thanksgiving Luncheon at the Intuit Dome on Friday, November 7, 2025. Seniors
will depart from the Inglewood Senior Center at approximately 11:15 a.m. and will be
transported to the Intuit Dome by buses generously provided by Intuit. We are deeply
grateful for their continued partnership and dedication to our senior community. Our
seniors look forward to enjoying a wonderful meal, festive fellowship, and the opportunity
to take photos with players during this special annual event. 5310 Grant Application to
Replace Community Services Buses - The City is in the process of applying for the Federal
Transit Administration (FTA) Section 5310 Grant, which provides funding to improve
mobility for seniors and individuals with disabilities. This grant supports the replacement
of older vehicles and other transportation-related enhancements. Eligible applicants
include public agencies and qualified non-profit organizations whose projects are included
in a locally developed, coordinated transportation plan. Funding may be used for capital
purchases (such as new buses), operating support, and mobility management initiatives.
Emergency Operations Center (EOC) Training for Upcoming Major Events - The Inglewood
Office of Emergency Services is conducting Emergency Operations Center (EOC) training
sessions to prepare staff for effective coordination and communication during
emergencies and large-scale events. With Inglewood set to host major events including
the World Cup, NBA All-Star Game, Super Bowl 2027, and the Olympic Games, these
trainings are essential to ensuring citywide readiness. The Parks, Recreation and
Community Services Department leadership team is actively engaged in these sessions,
strengthening their knowledge and preparedness to respond when needed.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Beck commended Mary Rouzan and her
team at Rogers Parks for their role in hosting the voting pole. He recommended honoring
Tony Kelley of Darby Park for his 30 years of service and retirement. He is also interested
in possibly adding a second season per year for basketball at the parks. Commissioner
Denmon addressed coyote breeding and future concerns if not addressed in a timely
manner.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:55p.m.
